chapter: Army, return to El Paso and Mardi Gras parades
title: The 1941 band photograph and who sat in the band
summary: Allen asks about a 1941 photo of Alfred's El Paso band; Watts says they used no bass or guitar, mostly piano and drums.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: This is Real 4 Bob Watts, February the 28th, 1963. There are some things I wanted to ask you about. I'll go right ahead. One thing, he showed me a picture of the band in 1941, Alfred did, in fact we got it up at school, with Melvin Wright and Jack Richards, a white talent player, and Martínez on piano. And did y'all have a guitar or a bass or anything in that band? There's a guy sitting on the stand and I can't see where his instruments.
No, no, we never used a bass. But sometime a bass player would come in and set in.
It couldn't have been a singer though, you had singers in the band.
And somebody was sitting up there by Alfred, the drummer?
I don't remember where he was sitting.
Well if he was sitting up there, that's a friend of ours on a big farm and ranch, that's Fred Scott. He used to come in quite often and sit up there and listen at his play.
I think it was a colored guy.
That could have been Fred Scott, yeah.
I just wondered, maybe Alfred will know. But you didn't use a bass.
No, we never had no bass, no guitar. Just piano and drum mostly.
